question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}$. If $C = 2A - B'$, find the matrix $C$ and identify its type (if possible).
explanation:
First, compute $2A$:

$2A = 2 \times \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}4 & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{bmatrix}$

Next, compute $B'$, the transpose of $B$:

$B' = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2\end{bmatrix}$

Now, find $C = 2A - B'$:

$C = \begin{bmatrix}4 & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2\end{bmatrix}$

$C = \begin{bmatrix}4-1 & -2-2 \\ 0-4 & 6-(-2)\end{bmatrix}$

$C = \begin{bmatrix}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{bmatrix}$

Observe that $C$ is a square matrix. Check if it is symmetric:

$C' = \begin{bmatrix}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{bmatrix} = C$

So $C$ is a symmetric matrix.

options.C: $C=\begin{bmatrix}5&2\\4&4\end{bmatrix}$ and $C$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric
